podcast.body: The band Tuftarts, which played on bills with the Ramones, was described as "sort of a direct descendant of sniper," indicating a lineage or influence. "Tuftarts, which, if you want to get technical about it, was sort of a direct descendant of sniper, Joey's old band."

podcast.title: Joey Ramone's First Band
podcast.body: This was Joey Ramone's first "real band," where he performed as the singer under the name Jeff Starship. They were active from 1972 to 1974 and specialized in writing songs about "weirdness and perversion." No known recordings exist of Joey Ramone's version of the band. "His first real band was called Sniper. Joey was their singer, going by the name Jeff Starship. And he specialized in running songs about weirdness and perversion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pre-Ramones Band – Jeff Hyman's Role
podcast.body: Jeff Hyman, who would later become Joey Ramone, formed a band called Sniper. In this group, he not only played the drums but also served as the singer, showcasing his dual talents before the formation of The Ramones. "Finally, he formed a band called Sniper and as well as playing the drums he ended up being the singer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation of the Band
xref.body: The four original members connected through a series of introductions: Jeffrey Hyman (Joey) met Douglas Colvin (Dee Dee) at a Sniper show; Douglas introduced Jeffrey to John Cummings (Johnny); and Johnny introduced them to Tommy Erdelyi (Tommy), who already knew Joey from the neighborhood. Tommy suggested they form a band, offering to manage them, which they did. "It was Tommy that told the other three guys that they should form a band, all advise and manage. And so they did."

xref.title: Joey Ramone's Early Glam Phase
xref.body: Around his 21st birthday, Joey became deeply immersed in glam culture, idolizing David Bowie and Alice Cooper. He would dress in satin jumpsuits adorned with rhinestones and wear knee-high platform boots, which exaggerated his height to six feet eight inches. "He also became a big fan of Alice Cooper. His first real band was called Sniper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Original Lineup and Roles
xref.body: The initial lineup included Jeff Hyman (Joey Ramone) on drums, a "6'6-inch skinny guy" and "OCD-suffering refugee from a failed band called Sniper." Their first gig was in March. By July, Jeff Hyman moved to lead vocals because he was a better singer than drummer, and their manager, Tommy (Tommy Ramone), a recording engineer who had worked with Jimi Hendrix, took over on drums. "Their drummer was a 6'6-inch skinny guy named Jeff Heimann, an OCD-suffering refugee from a failed band called Sniper."

xref.title: Shared Bills with Ramones
xref.body: In 1975, Tuftarts performed on bills with the Ramones at CBGB. The band was also described as being "sort of a direct descendant of sniper," Joey Ramone's old band, indicating a lineage within the punk scene. "Other times, they'd be on a bill with a talking heads or blondey or a band called Tuftarts, which, if you want to get technical about it, was sort of a direct descendant of sniper, Joey's old band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Transition from Drummer to Singer – Founding The Ramones
xref.body: In early 1974, Jeff Hyman was playing drums and singing in a band called Sniper. He then connected with John Cummings (guitar) and Douglas Colvin (bass), forming a new group that played its first gig on March 30, 1974. However, Hyman's drumming was too loud and fast for the band, and he proved to be a better singer than his bandmates. He moved to frontman, adopting the name Joey Ramone, while a friend named Tommy took over on a $100 drum set. "Jeff moved down front and became the singer and a friend named Tommy was forced to keep time using a hundred dollar drum set."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
